name: Patroclus
description: Achilles' beloved companion whose death in battle spurred the hero back to action.

name: Diomedes
description: A valiant Greek hero who, with Athena's help, wounded two gods during the Trojan War.

name: Priam
description: The elderly king of Troy who pleaded with Achilles for the return of his son Hector's body.

name: Paris
description: The Trojan prince whose abduction of Helen sparked the Trojan War.

name: Menelaus
description: The king of Sparta and abandoned husband of Helen, a key leader of the Greek forces.

name: Agamemnon
description: The commander-in-chief of the Achaean army and king of Mycenae.

name: Cassandra
description: A Trojan princess cursed by Apollo to utter true prophecies that no one would ever believe.

name: Hector
description: The greatest warrior of Troy, who was ultimately slain by Achilles.

name: Charon
description: The grim ferryman who transported the souls of the dead across the River Styx.

name: Thanatos
description: The personification of death, who could be tricked by clever mortals like Sisyphus.

name: Hypnos
description: The personification of sleep and twin brother of Thanatos.

name: Minos
description: A legendary king of Crete who became one of the three judges of the dead in the afterlife.

name: Rhadamanthus
description: A wise king who, after death, became a judge of the dead in the Underworld alongside Minos.

name: Erebus
description: The primordial deity of darkness, whose name was often used for the Underworld itself.

name: Nyx
description: The primordial goddess of the night, a shadowy figure of exceptional power and beauty.

name: The Furies
description: Chthonic deities of vengeance who pursued and punished wrongdoers, especially those guilty of patricide.

name: Niobe
description: A queen whose fourteen children were killed by Apollo and Artemis as punishment for her hubris.

name: Marsyas
description: A satyr who was flayed alive for daring to challenge Apollo to a music contest.

name: Actaeon
description: A hunter who was turned into a stag by Artemis and killed by his own hounds.

name: Pentheus
description: A king of Thebes who was torn apart by Maenads for spurning the worship of Dionysus.

name: Semele
description: A mortal lover of Zeus who was tricked by Hera into being incinerated by his divine form.

name: Io
description: A priestess of Hera whom Zeus turned into a heifer to hide her from his jealous wife.

name: Callisto
description: A nymph of Artemis who was turned into a bear by a jealous Hera or a vengeful Artemis.

name: Tityos
description: A giant eternally punished in Tartarus with two vultures eating his liver for assaulting Leto.

name: Bellerophon
description: The hero who tamed the winged horse Pegasus and slew the Chimera.

name: Theseus
description: The mythical king of Athens who navigated the Labyrinth to kill the Minotaur.

name: Cadmus
description: The founder of Thebes, who killed a sacred dragon and sowed its teeth to grow an army.

name: Meleager
description: A hero who organized a group of heroes to hunt and kill the Calydonian Boar.

name: Atalanta
description: A swift-footed huntress who was the first to draw blood in the Calydonian Boar hunt.

name: Oedipus
description: A tragic king of Thebes, famous for solving the riddle of the Sphinx.

name: Jason
description: The leader of the Argonauts in the quest for the Golden Fleece.

name: Heracles
description: The greatest of Greek heroes, who completed twelve labors and later ascended to godhood.

name: Amphitrite
description: A sea goddess and wife of Poseidon, often depicted with a trident or in a chariot of sea-horses.

name: Triton
description: The son of Poseidon and Amphitrite, a merman who used a conch shell as a trumpet.

name: Nereus
description: The 'Old Man of the Sea,' a Titan god of the sea known for his wisdom and prophetic abilities.

name: Thetis
description: A sea-nymph, leader of the Nereids, and the mother of the hero Achilles.

name: Galatea
description: A beautiful sea-nymph who was loved by the Cyclops Polyphemus.

name: Scylla
description: A sea monster who lived on one side of a narrow strait, opposite her counterpart Charybdis.

name: Charybdis
description: A sea monster who took the form of a giant whirlpool, threatening passing ships.

name: Odysseus
description: The clever king of Ithaca whose ten-year journey home from Troy was fraught with peril.

name: Daphne
description: A nymph who, fleeing from Apollo, was transformed into a laurel tree to escape him.

name: Arachne
description: A mortal weaver who was turned into a spider after challenging the goddess Athena.

name: Tiresias
description: A blind prophet of Apollo who was transformed into a woman for seven years.

name: Philomela
description: A princess who was transformed into a nightingale after suffering a horrific assault.

name: Procne
description: A sister of Philomela who was transformed into a swallow after taking revenge on her husband.

name: Lycaon
description: A king of Arcadia whom Zeus turned into a wolf as punishment for his wickedness.

name: Ascalaphus
description: An underworld daemon who was turned into an owl for revealing Persephone had eaten pomegranate seeds.

name: Proteus
description: A prophetic 'Old Man of the Sea' who could change his shape to avoid answering questions.

name: Leda
description: A Spartan queen who was seduced by Zeus in the form of a swan, mothering Helen and Pollux.

name: Danaë
description: A princess who was impregnated by Zeus in a shower of gold, giving birth to the hero Perseus.

name: Pasiphaë
description: The queen of Crete who, under a divine curse, gave birth to the monstrous Minotaur.

name: Echidna
description: A half-woman, half-snake creature known as the 'Mother of All Monsters'.

name: Typhon
description: A monstrous giant and the 'Father of All Monsters,' who challenged Zeus for supremacy.

name: Leto
description: A Titan goddess who gave birth to the divine twins Apollo and Artemis.

name: Maia
description: The eldest of the Pleiades and the mother of the god Hermes by Zeus.

name: Alcmene
description: A mortal princess who was tricked by Zeus and became the mother of the hero Heracles.

name: Hestia
description: The virgin goddess of the hearth, home, and family, who gave up her Olympian seat for Dionysus.

name: Hephaestus
description: The god of blacksmiths, craftsmen, and fire, known for being lame and married to Aphrodite.

name: Ares
description: The god of war, representing the violent and untamed aspects of battle.

name: Artemis
description: The goddess of the hunt, the wilderness, wild animals, and chastity.

name: Hermes
description: The messenger of the gods, known for his winged sandals and role as a guide to the Underworld.

name: Demeter
description: The goddess of the harvest and agriculture, whose grief for her daughter Persephone creates winter.

name: Dionysus
description: The god of wine, festivity, and theatre, who was the last god to be accepted on Olympus.

name: Apollo
description: The god of music, arts, knowledge, prophecy, and light, often associated with the Oracle at Delphi.

name: Zeus
description: King of the gods, ruler of the sky, and a serial shapeshifter to pursue his many romantic interests.

name: Hera
description: Queen of the gods and goddess of marriage, women, and childbirth, known for her jealousy.

name: Poseidon
description: God of the sea, earthquakes, and horses, one of the three most powerful Olympian gods.

name: Athena
description: Goddess of wisdom, courage, and strategic warfare, who sprang fully grown from Zeus's head.

name: Hades
description: God of the dead and king of the Underworld, though not technically an Olympian as he did not reside there.

name: Persephone
description: Queen of the Underworld, who was abducted by Hades and whose return to the surface brings spring.

name: Sisyphus
description: A king punished in Tartarus to eternally roll a boulder up a hill, only for it to roll down every time.

name: Tantalus
description: A king punished in Tartarus to stand in a pool of water beneath a fruit tree, with both receding from his grasp.

name: Perseus
description: The hero who slew Medusa and rescued Andromeda from a sea monster.

name: Achilles
description: The greatest Greek warrior at Troy, invulnerable except for his heel.

name: Medusa
description: A Gorgon with snakes for hair who could turn men to stone, once a beautiful priestess.

name: Helen
description: The most beautiful woman in the world, whose abduction by Paris caused the Trojan War.

name: Prometheus
description: A Titan who was punished by Zeus for stealing fire and giving it to mankind.

name: Icarus
description: The son of the master craftsman Daedalus, who flew too close to the sun with wings of wax and feathers.

name: Cerberus
description: The multi-headed dog that guarded the gates of the Underworld to prevent the dead from leaving.
